title: Cutsgunsuck
summary: Cutsgunsuck is Tooker's Indigenous placename for the brook or creek known in English as Stony Brook. The waterway marked part of the boundary between Brookhaven and Smithtown at the village of Stony Brook.
address_label: Stony Brook waterway / Brookhaven-Smithtown boundary, NY
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Cutsgunsuck, Cussquontuck, and Cutscwontock. The name is interpreted as stony brook or the stony creek, from a word for stone joined to a word for brook, outlet, creek, or tidal stream.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names carry the stories of the land and its people, reflecting the unbroken relationships between them.”

— The Decolonial Atlas, Turtle Island Decolonized (n.d.), Opening text, first sentence
land_loss_content: Cutsgunsuck shows that the familiar English name Stony Brook sits over an older Indigenous place description for the same waterway. The boundary history also points to how Native geography was reused in colonial patents, town records, and later municipal lines.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker associates Cutsgunsuck with a boundary creek in the modern Stony Brook waterway and village area. The exact historic creek course remains uncertain.
